title: Canada Confident of Final Trade Pact Text Before Modi's December Visit, Envoy Says
excerpt: High Commissioner Christopher Cooter told TOI the sixth round of CEPA talks is under way, ratification will take time, and Canada is 'far beyond a reset' with India — including on student caps, which he said are nowhere near being met.
body:
• Canada's high commissioner to India, Christopher Cooter, said Ottawa is confident the final text of the India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) will be ready ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Canada.
  • The sixth round of CEPA negotiations is taking place this week in New Delhi; an announcement that talks have concluded is expected during Modi's December 11-12 visit to Toronto and Ottawa, though ratification would take longer because provincial governments are involved.
  • For the diaspora reader: Canada is also looking at subsidiary agreements to facilitate business travel, and Cooter said the student caps that worried Indian families were aimed at fraudulent colleges — the caps, he said, are nowhere near being met.
  • Canada and India aim to more than double two-way goods and services trade to C$70 billion a year by 2030, from C$30.4 billion in 2025.

Canada is confident it can finalise the text of its long-negotiated trade pact with India before Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits next month, the country's high commissioner to India, Christopher Cooter, said in an interaction with Times of India editors. The sixth round of negotiations on the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) is under way this week, and Cooter said an announcement of the successful conclusion of the talks during Modi's December 11-12 visit would mark a milestone in the relationship.

Final text first, ratification later

Cooter was careful to separate the two steps. The actual ratification, he said, would take some time because provincial governments are involved, but he was confident the final text would be there. He added that Canada is also looking at subsidiary agreements that would facilitate business travel, and that many other announcements were expected from the visit, including in space. Negotiators have been working at an unusual pace: the sixth round in New Delhi comes barely a month after the fifth round in Ottawa, with Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu leading his team in person, as The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Among the issues being resolved are predictable market access for Canadian pulses, greater access for services, and more visas for Indian workers and students.

"It's not a reset. It is far beyond a reset."

— Christopher Cooter, Canada's high commissioner to India

What he told Indian students

Cooter also addressed the anxiety among Indian families about Canada's international student policies. Canada is home to roughly 300,000 Indian students. He said the perception that Canada had closed its doors was a misperception: the official caps were targeted at fraudulent, fly-by-night institutions rather than legitimate applicants, the caps are nowhere near being met, and in his assessment this is a good time to apply as a prospective Indian student.

How far the relationship has come

Cooter, who arrived in India in September 2025, described a recovery that began fragile and tentative and then accelerated after the leaders engaged. When Foreign Minister Anita Anand visited India last month and called on Modi, he said, the prime minister described it as the fastest acceleration in the relationship. The CEPA talks were formally launched in March this year by Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and Minister Sidhu in the presence of Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. If the December announcement lands, legal vetting and formal ratification would follow.
